background: Badalona, Spain native and the first Spanish-born NBA head coach. Began in Spain's youth system and Cleveland's player-development program (2009), coached the Canton Charge (G League) to a 2014-15 Eastern Conference title, then served as an NBA assistant with Cleveland (2016-19), Denver (2019-22) and as Mike Brown's associate head coach in Sacramento (2022-24), where the Kings posted a record offensive rating and snapped a 16-year playoff drought. As Canada's national team head coach he went 6-2 at the 2023 FIBA World Cup, beating Team USA for the bronze medal, and led Canada at the 2024 Olympics. Hired by Brooklyn in April 2024 to steer a full rebuild: 26-56 in 2024-25 and 20-62 in 2025-26 with five first-round rookies, yet the Nets extended him and his staff in April 2026. Identity: extreme three-point volume ('50 threes a game'), ball and body movement, and an aggressive, blitz-and-switch, turnover-forcing defense.

record_last5.notes: Not a head coach; Nuggets assistant under Michael Malone.
Associate head coach under Mike Brown; Kings' record offensive rating; playoff drought ended.
Also coached Canada to 2023 World Cup bronze in the preceding summer.
First season; overachieved early (sixth-best ORtg through five games) before deadline sell-off; Cam Thomas career-high scoring.
Five first-round rookies (Demin, Traore, Powell, Saraf, Wolf); last in points per game (105.9) and tied-last in 3P% (34%); 7-4 in December 2025; extension April 2026.
Early-season record not retrievable in this research pass; early reporting noted opponents posting the league's highest eFG% (58.1) against Brooklyn.

evidence: Rebuilding rosters with five rookies produced 10-11 man rotations in 2025-26; started three rookies with Porter Jr. and Clowney out and won at Utah.
Rookie minutes were still rationed: Demin led the class at about 18.9 mpg early in 2025-26, drawing criticism that the bench was too deep with vets.
No true star to ride; Michael Porter Jr. was the primary scorer at a moderate load in 2025-26, and Cam Thomas's minutes were handled cautiously on return from a hamstring injury (Nov 2025).
Fernandez pulled Thomas after 21 minutes mid-fourth quarter in a 2024-25 game vs Cleveland.
Frequent lineup experimentation: three-rookie starting groups, 'three unique lineups' previews, and in-season shifts of the initiator role to Porter Jr. (2025-26).
Opinion piece (Sep 2026) asked whether the Nets can 'play different lineups in close 4th quarters', implying continued churn.
Columnists in Nov-Dec 2025 said the Nets had 'a glaring problem regarding rookie minutes' and should 'lean into youth' even at the cost of losses; Fernandez prefers that minutes be earned.
Yet rookies closed and won a game at Utah, and Fernandez insists his rookies shoot threes to develop: 'Nets HC explains why his rookies need to shoot threes'.
Rebuilding context: veterans were traded or rested and injured players (Thomas) brought back on restrictions; no evidence of resting healthy stars for its own sake (inferred).
Rookies closed the Utah win (2025-26); Fernandez has subbed Thomas out of fourth quarters and rotated closers by matchup and effort.
Fernandez has tied late minutes to effort: criticized 'atrocious' late effort after a collapse vs Milwaukee (2024).
SI: 'Jordi Fernandez's high-paced vision for the Nets isn't going according to plan' - outlet passes stuck in Porter Jr./Mann's hands and tempo lagged (2025-26).
Fernandez defines pace in the half court: 'I think our pace in the halfcourt is good based on ball movement and body movement' (Nov 2024).
'Jordi Fernandez wants Nets to shoot 50 threes a game' (SI, 2024-25); attempts rose nearly three per game immediately after he arrived and the team ranked 2nd in catch-and-shoot attempts.
2025-26 preview: Nets 'poised to lean on the three even more'; he insists rookies shoot threes.
Early 2024-25 Nets were near the top of the league in passes per game with the sixth-best offensive rating; Fernandez credited 'unselfishness'.
Drifted toward Porter Jr. initiating more in 2025-26 (career-high 24.2 ppg) as rookies struggled to create.
'Sometimes, the defense fuels your offense' - turnover-forcing scheme meant to create fast breaks (2024-25).
Stated high-pace vision not fully realized; ball stuck after outlet passes (2025-26).
Five-out, high-3PA structure with floor-spacing bigs (Clowney, Wolf) implies limited crashing; Claxton/Sharpe provide some second-chance work (inferred; no team rank retrieved).
Fernandez called a midrange-heavy shot diet 'pretty awful' after a loss to Detroit and wants rim-or-three shots; post-ups are rare.
SI: 'Brooklyn Nets HC Jordi Fernandez (on) midrange shot diet' - explicit preference against long twos.
Pedigree as Sacramento's offensive associate (record ORtg, 2022-23) and Canada's bronze-medal coach; Mike Brown called him 'the right guy' to lead a rebuild.
No independent ATO efficiency reporting found; Nets finished last in scoring in 2025-26 with a talent-poor roster.
'Runs an aggressive defensive scheme and often blitzes the pick-and-roll ball handler'; principles include 'heavy switches, double teams, and fullcourt pressure' (SI, 2025).
Nets forced about 15 turnovers per game during a 2024-25 surge; Lichtenstein: the 'hard-hedge version depends on perimeter defenders applying ball pressure without fouling'.

Ball pressure, blitzing and switching push the defense toward the perimeter; Nets allowed the 3rd-fewest points in the paint in 2025-26 (Roundtable, Oct 2026) but opponents' eFG% was the league's highest early in 2026-27, suggesting open threes are the cost.
Fernandez (Dec 2024): team 'did not effectively pressure the ball and were out of balance on defensive rotations' when it failed.

Scheme success explicitly hinges on 'ball pressure without fouling' (Lichtenstein), and a young, blitzing roster has been foul-prone (inferred from scheme and roster; no opponent FT-rate rank retrieved).
Comes from Mike Brown's Sacramento staff, which used zone liberally, and used zone looks with Canada; Nets have mixed in occasional zone but no reporting quantifies it (inferred).
Mixes blitz, hard hedge and switching by opponent; moved Wagner into a 'different role' on defense in 2026 camp; regretted a late double-team scheme vs Giannis (2024).
Base identity remains consistently aggressive regardless of personnel, which has cost him when the roster lacks a rim protector.
Lichtenstein (2024-25): Fernandez was 'sometimes slow to call timeouts on opponent runs', though framed as a minor complaint.
Blown fourth-quarter leads vs Atlanta and Milwaukee drew attention to his run management.
After a loss to Boston he lamented a possession up five where 'we had a chance to foul the big man' - indicates he actively considers intentional fouling to protect late leads (2025-26).
Mixed: has closed with rookies (Utah win) and also pulled scorers (Thomas) late; no consistent shrink-to-six pattern documented (inferred).
Lost a late out-of-bounds challenge vs New Orleans that handed the Pelicans possession up 112-110 with 11 seconds left (2025-26); no aggregate success-rate data found.
Analytics-oriented coach from an analytics-heavy Sacramento staff; no direct evidence on 2-for-1 hunting (inferred).
Chose to double Giannis Antetokounmpo in the decisive stretch of a 2024 loss and later regretted it; aggressive defensive gambles carry into late-game choices.
'There's no safe lead in the NBA' after nearly blowing a late lead vs Chicago (Jan 2026).
Multiple blown fourth-quarter leads (Hawks, Bucks) and late defensive breakdowns (Hugo Gonzalez tying shot with 0.4 left vs Boston) on talent-poor rosters.
Fernandez himself said the team had 'executed late-game well in many games' but two situations vs Boston 'could have gone better'.
Shifted initiator duties to Porter Jr., expanded Thomas's playmaking role, and re-cast Wagner defensively; December 2025 7-4 stretch credited to adjustments.
Core scheme (blitz/high 3PA) stays fixed even when personnel do not fit, which analysts flagged in 2025-26.
Cam Thomas's career year (2024-25), Porter Jr.'s career-high 24.2 ppg (2025-26), growth of Jalen Wilson, Day'Ron Sharpe and Noah Clowney; GM Sean Marks called him 'a tremendous leader'.
Rookie class development was debated in 2025-26 because of limited minutes.
Explicit shot-diet language ('50 threes a game', midrange 'pretty awful'), top-tier catch-and-shoot frequency and a turnover-forcing defense all reflect analytics-driven design.
Formed in Sacramento's data-forward staff under Mike Brown.
'NBA analysts praise Nets' Jordi Fernandez' despite projecting a shockingly low win total; reportedly 'impressed plenty of coaches around the NBA'; extended with his whole staff in April 2026.
46-118 two-year record led some to question the extension (Bleacher Report, 2026).

key_criticisms: 46-118 over two seasons; 2025-26 Nets finished last in scoring (105.9 ppg) and tied-last in 3P% (34%) while attempting a very high volume of threes.
Rationed rookie minutes in 2025-26 despite a five-rookie rebuild, drawing 'lean into youth' criticism from beat writers.
Aggressive blitz/switch scheme leaks open threes and fouls when the roster lacks a rim protector; opponents' eFG% was the league's highest early in 2026-27.
Sometimes slow to stop opponent runs with timeouts; several blown fourth-quarter leads.
key_strengths: Clear, modern offensive identity: extreme three-point volume, drive-and-kick, elite early-season passing numbers in 2024-25.
Aggressive, turnover-forcing defense (blitz, hedge, switch, full-court pressure) that punches above the roster's talent in stretches (7-4 December 2025).
Respected developer and communicator: Canada bronze medal, Mike Brown's endorsement, staff-wide extension in April 2026.
Analytics-literate shot-diet discipline and willingness to speak bluntly about effort and shot quality.
research_notes: Records 26-56 (2024-25) and 20-62 (2025-26) confirmed by Wikipedia, AP/Hoops Rumors and StatMuse; the 2026-27 opening record was not retrievable before the search budget ran out. Canton Charge record is approximate (background knowledge). No full-season pace, 3PA-rate, offensive-rebound or opponent-FT-rate rankings could be pulled (stats sites blocked); 3PA volume is well documented qualitatively but the exact 2025-26 rank is not. Zone usage, 2-for-1 behavior and offensive rebounding are inferred (no sources) and carry confidence <= 0.3. A Hoops Rumors item suggested Cam Thomas left the Nets during or after 2025-26; details and timing were not verified. Some search results (e.g., 'lightstar' and 'bottegadelsarto' pages) were discarded as unreliable/synthetic.
